text: Walk for 1–2 minutes. If you can, do an easy 5-minute walk.
March in place for 60 seconds. Light and steady.
Do 15–25 calf raises. Slow up, slow down.
Ankles: 10 circles each direction per foot.
Hands on hips: 5–8 gentle back extensions. Stop if it hurts.
Stand tall and shift weight left/right for 60 seconds.
Do 10 slow hip hinges. Keep your back neutral.
Glute squeeze: 3 sec on, 3 sec off. Repeat 10 times.
Roll shoulders back and down 8 times. Keep the neck soft.
Posture reset: feet flat, hips back, ribs down, head over shoulders.
Chin tuck: gently pull chin straight back. Hold 2 sec x 8.
Squeeze shoulder blades gently. 10 reps, no lower-back arch.
Look far away for 20 seconds and blink slowly.
Refocus: far object then near object. Repeat 5 times.
3 slow breaths: inhale 4 sec, exhale 6 sec. Drop shoulders.
Shake out your hands for 20 seconds. Loosen your grip.
Drink a few sips of water, then walk a quick lap.
Just ate? A short walk now is extra helpful.
Standing still isn’t the goal. Movement is.
Keep it tiny but real: 60 seconds of moving is a win.
Walk to the door/window and back 2–3 times.
Do 10–15 gentle high-knee steps (no bouncing).
Stand tall and ‘grow’ through the top of your head for 10 seconds.
On each exhale, lightly brace your abs. Repeat 5 times.
Small steps forward/back for 60 seconds. Controlled pace.
Skip intense stretching. Choose gentle movement instead.
Shrug up for 2 sec, then relax down. Repeat 6 times.
Wall ‘W’: elbows back, slow reps x 8.
Very gentle head turns left/right. 3 each side.
Stop the ‘forward head’: chin back 2 sec x 6.
Close eyes for 5 seconds, then do 5 slow blinks.
Make the exhale longer than the inhale for 3 breaths.
Get fresh air for 30 seconds if you can.
Quick check: screen near eye level, feet supported, back supported.
Relax the hands: keep elbows close, wrists neutral.
The break is part of the work. It keeps you effective.
Sit-to-stand: 8–10 reps to a chair. If unsure, just walk.
Wall push-ups: 8–12 reps. Smooth and easy.
Heel-to-toe rocking for 30–40 seconds.
Pain or numbness = stop. Choose easy walking only.
Walk a quick loop around the room. Keep it easy.
Do 20–30 seconds of gentle side steps. No bouncing.
Toe taps: alternate feet for 30–40 seconds.
Stand on one foot for 10 seconds each side. Hold a desk if needed.
Hip circles: small, slow circles 5 each direction.
Mini lunge step-back: 5 each side, shallow and controlled.
Hands on thighs: gentle cat-cow while standing. 6 slow reps.
Pelvic tilt: tuck and release gently. 8 reps.
Exhale and gently tighten your lower abs for 3 seconds. Repeat 6 times.
Tall posture + slow breath: brace lightly on the exhale. 4 breaths.
Shoulder blade circles: slow and small, 6 each way.
Reach up, then relax down. 5 reps, no rib flare.
Wall angels: slow slides up/down. 6 reps (only if comfy).
Elbows at sides: pull back gently like you’re rowing. 10 reps.
Neck reset: imagine a string lifting the crown of your head for 5 seconds.
Ear-to-shoulder: tiny range, 2 reps each side. Stop if it pinches.
Open/close fists slowly 10 times. Relax between reps.
Wrist circles: 8 each direction. Keep it gentle.
Finger spread: spread wide for 2 sec, relax. Repeat 8 times.
Posture cue: stack ears over shoulders over hips. Hold 10 seconds.
Do the 20-20-20: look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Blink drill: 10 slow blinks. Let the eyes fully close.
Look up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right. One slow round.
Relax your brow and jaw. Then refocus on a far object for 15 seconds.
Box-ish breath: inhale 4, hold 2, exhale 6. Repeat 3 times.
Sigh out: one long exhale through the mouth, then breathe normally.
Breathe into the sides of your ribs for 3 slow breaths.
Ask: what’s the next tiny step? Do only that after the break.
Drop tension: unclench jaw, soften tongue, relax shoulders.
Stand up, drink water, then take 10 calm steps. Done.
Quick reset: pull the screen a bit farther away if you’re leaning in.
Lower your shoulders and bring elbows closer to your body.
Check brightness: match screen brightness to the room (no glare).
Increase font size by 1 step if you’re squinting.
Mouse grip check: loosen your grip and rest the hand between moves.
Stand and do 10 heel raises, then 10 toe raises.
Chair optional: sit down for 20 seconds, then stand back up calmly.
Foot pumps: alternate pointing and flexing toes 12 times each foot.
Glute tap: lightly tap glutes with your hands, then do 6 squeezes.
Hinge to desk: hands on desk, hips back, long spine. Hold 5 seconds.
Hands behind head: elbows wide, breathe out and gently open chest. 3 breaths.
‘Shoulders in pockets’: slide them down and back for 5 seconds.
Chin tuck + slow exhale. 5 reps.
Ribs down, pelvis neutral, head tall. Hold 10 seconds.
Open a window or change air for 30 seconds if possible.
If you’re stuck: write one sentence about what you’re doing next.
Keep it pain-free. If something feels sharp, skip it.
Dizzy? Sit down, breathe slowly, and keep the break gentle.
No deep stretches during breaks. Light motion is enough.
Make it easy: 60 seconds of walking beats ‘perfect’ every time.
Look at something green/natural (tree/plant) for 20 seconds.
Drop your gaze to the floor for 10 seconds, then look far again.
Thumb stretch: gently pull thumb back with the other hand. 5 seconds each.
Forearm shake-out: loose wrists, 15 seconds.
Count 3 breaths. On each exhale, let the shoulders drop.
Return calmer: pick one task, mute the rest for 10 minutes.
Screen height check: top of screen near eye level (no neck crane).
Feet check: both feet supported. If not, reposition before continuing.
Two-minute stroll if you can. Even short breaks help.
Quick tidy: clear one small item from your desk, then move for 20 seconds.
